galaxies.name: Andromeda Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way and is on a collision course with it in about 4 billion years.

galaxies.name: Sombrero Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Sombrero Galaxy is known for its bright nucleus and large central bulge, giving the appearance of a sombrero hat.

galaxies.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Whirlpool Galaxy is a classic spiral galaxy interacting with a smaller companion galaxy, producing spectacular spiral arm structures.

galaxies.name: Pinwheel Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Pinwheel Galaxy is well known for its large size and grand design spiral arms visible even in amateur telescopes.

galaxies.name: Centaurus A
galaxies.description: Centaurus A is a peculiar galaxy known for its dust lane and radio emissions.

galaxies.name: Tadpole Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Tadpole Galaxy exhibits a long tidal tail from gravitational interactions with other galaxies.

galaxies.name: Messier 87
galaxies.description: Messier 87 is a giant elliptical galaxy with a supermassive black hole at its center.

galaxies.name: NGC 1300
galaxies.description: NGC 1300 is a barred spiral galaxy noted for its grand-design spiral arms.

galaxies.name: Cigar Galaxy
galaxies.description: The Cigar Galaxy is experiencing intense star formation and emits strong winds of gas.

galaxies.name: Messier 81
galaxies.description: Messier 81 is a spiral galaxy with well-defined arms and a supermassive black hole.

galaxies.name: NGC 6946
galaxies.description: NGC 6946 is known as the Fireworks Galaxy due to its frequent supernovae.

galaxies.name: NGC 2903
galaxies.description: NGC 2903 is a barred spiral galaxy with active star-forming regions.

galaxies.name: NGC 3310
galaxies.description: NGC 3310 has undergone a recent collision and is bursting with new stars.

galaxies.name: NGC 1365
galaxies.description: NGC 1365 is one of the most spectacular barred spiral galaxies known.

galaxies.name: Messier 63
galaxies.description: Also known as the Sunflower Galaxy, Messier 63 has a bright core and distinctive arms.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.description: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun. It has a rocky body with a cratered surface, very similar to Earth's moon.

planets.name: Venus
planets.description: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. It is a terrestrial planet and is sometimes called Earth's 'sister planet' because of their similar size, mass, and proximity to the Sun. It has a dense, toxic atmosphere.

planets.name: Earth
planets.description: Our home planet is the third planet from the Sun, and the only place we know of so far that's inhabited by living things. It is an ocean planet, with water covering 71% of its surface.

planets.name: Mars
planets.description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It is a dusty, cold, desert world with a very thin atmosphere. It is known as the 'Red Planet' due to the iron oxide prevalent on its surface.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.description: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system - more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined. It is famous for its Great Red Spot, a giant storm bigger than Earth.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.description: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest in the Solar System. It is adorned with a dazzling, complex system of icy rings.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.description: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun. It is an ice giant and has a unique tilt; it rotates on its side, making it appear to roll around the Sun like a barrel.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.description: Neptune—the eighth and most distant major planet orbiting our Sun—is dark, cold and whipped by supersonic winds. It was the first planet located through mathematical calculations.

exoplanets.name: Proxima Centauri b
exoplanets.description: The closest known exoplanet to our Solar System. It orbits within the habitable zone of a red dwarf star, meaning liquid water could theoretically exist on its surface.

exoplanets.name: TRAPPIST-1e
exoplanets.description: One of seven Earth-sized planets orbiting the ultra-cool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1. It is considered one of the most potentially habitable exoplanets discovered so far.

exoplanets.name: Kepler-186f
exoplanets.description: The first Earth-sized planet discovered in the habitable zone of another star. Because its star is cooler and redder than our Sun, any plant life there might appear red or black.

exoplanets.name: 55 Cancri e
exoplanets.description: A scorching hot 'super-Earth' that orbits its star so closely a year lasts only 18 hours. It is theorized to be covered in oceans of lava and possess a core made of diamond.

exoplanets.name: WASP-12b
exoplanets.description: A massive gas giant orbiting so close to its parent star that it is literally being torn apart and consumed by the star's gravity, stretching the planet into an egg shape.

exoplanets.name: Kepler-22b
exoplanets.description: The first planet confirmed by NASA's Kepler mission to orbit within the habitable zone of a Sun-like star. It is likely a 'water world' entirely covered by a global ocean.

exoplanets.name: HD 189733 b
exoplanets.description: A beautiful deep blue gas giant that hides a deadly secret: its weather includes winds blowing at 5,400 mph and horizontal rain made of jagged silicate glass.

exoplanets.name: PSR B1257+12 B
exoplanets.description: One of the very first exoplanets ever discovered. It orbits a pulsar—the rapidly spinning, dead core of an exploded star—making it a highly irradiated, desolate world.

blackHoles.name: Messier 87*
blackHoles.description: Famous for being the very first black hole to ever be directly imaged by humanity (using the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019). It weighs 6.5 billion times the mass of our Sun.

blackHoles.name: Sagittarius A*
blackHoles.description: The supermassive black hole at the very center of our own Milky Way galaxy. Despite its massive size, it is currently 'quiet' and not consuming large amounts of material.

blackHoles.name: Cygnus X-1
blackHoles.description: One of the strongest X-ray sources seen from Earth, and the first astronomical object widely accepted to be a black hole. It slowly strips material away from a massive blue companion star.

blackHoles.name: TON 618
blackHoles.description: One of the most massive black holes ever discovered in the universe, weighing an incomprehensible 66 billion times the mass of our Sun. It powers an incredibly bright quasar.

blackHoles.name: Gaia BH1
blackHoles.description: Currently the closest known black hole to Earth. It is a dormant black hole, meaning it is not actively feeding on its companion star, making it very difficult to detect.

blackHoles.name: V404 Cygni
blackHoles.description: A stellar-mass black hole known for unpredictable and dramatic outbursts of energy. It occasionally produces jets of particles moving at near light-speed.

blackHoles.name: Holmberg 15A
blackHoles.description: Located in the center of the Abell 85 galaxy cluster, it is one of the largest black holes ever measured dynamically, with a mass roughly 40 billion times that of the Sun.

blackHoles.name: J0313-1806
blackHoles.description: The most distant known quasar. Because it is so far away, we see it as it existed just 670 million years after the Big Bang, challenging our understanding of how quickly black holes can grow.
